title: The Moon in Silver Glory Shone
description: The Moon in Silver Glory Shone in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 85, “On the eclipse of the moon. July 30, 1776”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The moon in sil-ver glo-ry shone, And not a cloud in sight; When sud-den-ly a shade be-gun To in-ter-cept her light.

lines: The moon in silver glory shone,
And not a cloud in sight;
How fast across her orb it spread,
A circle, tinged with languid red,
Gaze on thy works in vain;
Assist me, Lord, that I may try
Fain would my thankful heart and lips
Thy peoples guilt, a heavy load!
Deprived thee of the light of God,
And filled thy soul with gloom.
Thus shall thy faithfulness and love,
Dark, like the moon without the sun,
For light or comfort I have none,
But lo! the hour draws near apace,
Then I shall see thee face to face,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
